title: Morning Headlines
intro: A Russian ballistic barrage kills civilians in Kyiv, a landmark Hamas disarmament deal takes its first tentative steps, Asian markets stage the biggest single-day surge in South Korean history, and a deadly border crisis unfolds at Spain's African enclave.

items.title: Russia Strikes Kyiv with Ballistic Missiles, Killing at Least 9
items.subtitle: Al Jazeera
items.summary: Russia fired 27 ballistic missiles at Ukraine's capital on August 1, with only one intercepted — Ukraine's Patriot air-defense stocks reportedly exhausted — killing nine people including children and wounding 33 more. The scale of the raid underscores Ukraine's deepening air-defense crisis as the war enters its fifth year.

items.title: Trump Calls Hamas Disarmament Agreement 'Historic' as Two-Week Ceasefire Begins
items.subtitle: Axios / CNN
items.summary: The US-led Board of Peace announced Hamas agreed to a phased 200–250-day disarmament process in Gaza, with militants beginning ceasefire terms on August 1; however, Israel has not publicly accepted its own withdrawal obligations, leaving the deal's durability in doubt.

items.title: South Korea's KOSPI Rockets 18% — Its Largest Single-Day Gain Ever
items.subtitle: Korea Times / Bloomberg
items.summary: Samsung Electronics surged 28% and SK Hynix hit its 30% daily limit-up as strong AI cloud-spending results from Microsoft and Amazon reversed a brutal three-day tech selloff driven by AI-bubble fears and rising Chinese chip competition; Japan's Nikkei and Taiwan's TAIEX also rose sharply.

items.title: Death Toll Reaches 67 in Spain's Ceuta Border Crisis with Morocco
items.subtitle: Euronews
items.summary: Dozens of migrants died — some drowning, others crushed in a stampede — while attempting to cross a breakwater barrier into Spain's North African exclave of Ceuta, making it one of the deadliest single migration incidents at the Spanish border in years and reigniting EU-Morocco tensions.

items.title: S&P 500 Rises 1% as Magnificent Seven Lead Tech Rebound; Index Up 9% for 2026
items.subtitle: Seeking Alpha / CNBC
items.summary: US equities recovered on August 1 — the Nasdaq gained 2.8% and the S&P 500 closed up 1% — as mega-cap tech stocks reversed a midweek Federal Reserve-driven selloff, with Wall Street's consensus year-end S&P 500 target now sitting at roughly 7,850.
